propositions: The 'undecomposed' hard-override axis fires on 0.1% of verified findings (11/10250 plan-v3, 18/11773 plan-v4), two orders of magnitude below every other severity axis.

The axis's deterministic suppressor (G5 veto) never fires in any of 2,000 reviewed sidecars, contradicting the stated justification that it correctly suppresses false flat-plan findings on childless tickets (90%+ of the population).

The axis's low-grade non-none findings (16 of 29 fires are 'low') are floored to impact 0.85 unconditionally, making 'low' == 'high' and causing low grades to block plans in isolation (sole override in 25/29 fires).

The inverse population (findings text-matching 'undecomposed' / 'flat plan' but graded 'none') is 33/10250 (plan-v3) and 17/11773 (plan-v4), but spot-checked samples are code-decomposition false positives, not missed plan-level defects.

The axis exhibits the same ordinal-ladder miscalibration already fixed in 'ac_unverifiable' (plan-v3) and 'divergent_implementation' (plan-v4): grading conservatively but flooring all non-none grades equally, causing weak signals to block.
